page: Amazon Web Services i4i.24xlarge is a storage-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 96 vCPUs derived from 48 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at up to 3.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system provides 768.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, offering an allocation ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU, alongside 54 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates 22,500 GB of dense local NVMe SSD storage and supports a baseline network bandwidth of 56 Gbps. No hardware accelerators or GPUs are included.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate strong multi-threaded compute capability and high memory bandwidth, placing the instance in the top 25% for multi-core stress-ng tests (92,861.79) and multi-core Geekbench performance (17,841.0). In cryptographic evaluations, hardware extensions such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI achieve top-tier tier results, reaching the top 10% in PassMark encryption metrics (87,228.27). In contrast, single-core benchmarks remain in the middle 50%, with a single-core stress-ng value of 1,891.49 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1,642.0. Large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 322.22 GB/sec uncached, paired with robust PassMark database performance of 29,810.64 operations.

Cost efficiency is focused around resource consolidation and local storage density. Combining 22.5 TB of local NVMe SSD storage with 96 vCPUs and 768 GB of RAM reduces the requirement for external storage attachments in high-throughput environments. The tradeoff lies in single-thread CPU performance and large-parameter LLM generation speeds, which fall into middle percentiles. Workloads that match this profile include large-scale transactional databases, in-memory caching systems such as Redis, distributed NoSQL databases, search index engines, and high-throughput static web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services i4i.24xlarge is a storage-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and an Intel Xeon 8375C processor. It provides 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores, 768.0 GB of DDR4 memory, and 22,500 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage, with baseline networking at 56 Gbps and no discrete GPUs. Benchmark results position the server in the top 25% for multi-core processing, database operations, and software compilation, alongside top 10% encryption test scores enabled by cryptographic instruction extensions. Single-core throughput and CPU-based LLM generation remain average. This resource profile offers strong efficiency for dense, I/O-intensive workloads requiring extensive memory and low-latency disk throughput, making it well-suited for distributed NoSQL databases, large transactional relational databases, high-capacity Redis caches, and static data processing platforms.
